examples.question_text:
Add and subtract these fractions.
a) $\frac{4}{9}+\frac{7}{9}$
b) $\frac{9}{13}-\frac{4}{13}$
examples.solution_text:
a) The parts are ninths, so add the numerators and keep the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{4}{9}+\frac{7}{9}\\&=\frac{11}{9}\end{aligned}$
b) The parts are thirteenths, so subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{9}{13}-\frac{4}{13}\\&=\frac{5}{13}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
a) Find the missing numerator: $\frac{\boxed{\rule{0pt}{5mm}\hspace{8mm}}}{15}-\frac{4}{15}=\frac{9}{15}$.
b) Calculate $\frac{8}{15}-\frac{2}{15}$. Simplify your answer.
examples.solution_text:
a) There must be $4$ more fifteenths than $9$ fifteenths.
$9+4=13$
The missing numerator is $13$.
b) Subtract the numerators and keep the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{8}{15}-\frac{2}{15}\\&=\frac{6}{15}\\&=\frac{2}{5}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
a) Calculate $\frac{7}{9}+\frac{8}{9}-\frac{2}{9}$. Leave your answer as an improper fraction.
b) Calculate $1-\frac{5}{12}$.
examples.solution_text:
a) Add and subtract the numerators from left to right.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{7}{9}+\frac{8}{9}-\frac{2}{9}\\&=\frac{15}{9}-\frac{2}{9}\\&=\frac{13}{9}\end{aligned}$
b) Write the whole as twelfths.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1-\frac{5}{12}\\&=\frac{12}{12}-\frac{5}{12}\\&=\frac{7}{12}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Lena eats $\frac{3}{10}$ of a cake. Omar eats $\frac{4}{10}$ of the same cake. What fraction of the cake is left?
examples.solution_text:
First find the fraction eaten.
$\frac{3}{10}+\frac{4}{10}=\frac{7}{10}$
Subtract this from the whole cake.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}1-\frac{7}{10}\\&=\frac{10}{10}-\frac{7}{10}\\&=\frac{3}{10}\end{aligned}$
